mainTopic: Whether חייבי כריתות get מלקות, and how the רבנן and רבי יצחק each find sources for counting forbidden relationships separately, for one woman with three names, and for a full sister.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why, according to the רבנן, a person who is חייב כרת can still get מלקות: כרת is never certain, because תשובה can erase it. Then it brings רבי יצחק, who learns from the extra mention of כרת for a sister that חייבי כריתות get כרת and not מלקות. The גמרא asks where each side learns that every forbidden relationship counts separately (לחלק), and concludes that both learn it from 'ואל אשה' in the פסוק about a נדה. According to the רבנן, the extra כרת for a sister then teaches a separate חיוב for one woman who is a man's sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister, a case that happens only with a רשע son of a רשע. For רבי יצחק, the גמרא first suggests a קל וחומר from רבי עקיבא's question about five נדות. It rejects that קל וחומר because it can be broken, and gives him the second 'אחותו' in the פסוק instead. The רבנן use that second 'אחותו' for a full sister, which teaches אין עונשין מן הדין. The amud ends while the גמרא is giving רבי יצחק's source for the full sister, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: תשובה can erase כרת, so מלקות still apply
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers, according to the רבנן, that כרת and מלקות do not clash, because תשובה makes the בית דין של מעלה forgive the כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we said at the start: if they do תשובה, the heavenly court forgives them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before: how can the רבנן give מלקות to someone who is already חייב כרת? It points back to what was said earlier, that תשובה can wipe away כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person does not get two punishments for one sin. But כרת is not a sure punishment, because the בית דין של מעלה forgives it if the sinner does תשובה. So the earthly מלקות is not a second, extra punishment on top of a certain one.

keyTerms.meaning: Repentance; returning to ה׳ after a sin
The heavenly court
They forgive or pardon
At the start; earlier on

phrases.english: As we said at the start,
that if they did repentance,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה מוֹחֲלִין לָהֶן.
phrases.english: the heavenly court forgives them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from just before this text: why, according to the רבנן, a person who is חייב כרת can also get מלקות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the two punishments do not clash, because כרת can be erased.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone who is חייב כרת should not get מלקות, since that would be two punishments for one sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since תשובה can erase כרת, the מלקות is not a double punishment.

steps.title: But these people did not repent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: we are talking about people who did not do תשובה, so their כרת is still in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say? But these people did not do תשובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge to the answer it just gave. If the sinner never did תשובה, the כרת stays, so we are back to two punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 1 only works if תשובה actually happened. The challenge says that in our case it did not, so the כרת is still there and the problem of double punishment comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: What would you say? A way of bringing up a possible objection
But look, here
They did

phrases.english: What would you say?
That these did not do repentance?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ? הָא לָא עֲבוּד תְּשׁוּבָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תשובה removes the clash between כרת and מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case before בית דין the sinner did not do תשובה, so the כרת is still in force.

steps.title: כרת is never certain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we can never be sure about כרת, because the person might do תשובה, so the מלקות still apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter is not clear-cut when it comes to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even if the person has not done תשובה yet, כרת is never a sure thing, so בית דין still gives מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against two punishments applies only when the second punishment is certain. כרת always stays open, since the sinner can do תשובה at any time. So מלקות are given, and the clash does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is not clear-cut or definite
A punishment from Heaven of being 'cut off'

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, a person who is חייב כרת can get מלקות, because כרת is never certain: תשובה can always erase it.

phrases.english: The matter is not clear-cut regarding karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the question from 'did he repent?' to 'is כרת ever certain?'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he did not repent, כרת is in force, so מלקות would be a double punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: כרת is never certain, so מלקות are given.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: כרת replaces מלקות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק holds that the separate mention of כרת for a man and his sister teaches that חייבי כריתות get כרת and not מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: all the חייבי כריתות were already included in the general rule. So why was כרת for a man with his sister mentioned on its own? To punish him with כרת and not with מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the view of רבי יצחק, which goes against the רבנן. He says a person who is חייב כרת gets only כרת, without מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general פסוק that gives כרת for all the forbidden relationships. Yet the תורה mentions כרת again just for a man and his sister. רבי יצחק says that this extra mention teaches a rule for all of them: the punishment is כרת, not מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are liable to כרת
They were already included in the general rule
It was taken out, meaning mentioned separately
Lashes given by בית דין

steps.confusionAlert: The case of the sister is singled out in order to teach a rule about all חייבי כריתות. It is not a special rule just for a sister.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
Those liable to karet were included in the general rule,
and why was karet for his sister taken out on its own?
To judge him with karet and not with lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opposing view to the רבנן discussed in steps 1 to 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייבי כריתות get כרת and not מלקות, learned from the extra mention of כרת for a sister.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from the sister verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the extra mention of כרת for a sister, since they do not use it the way רבי יצחק does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, why do they need כרת to be written for his sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן. They hold that חייבי כריתות do get מלקות, so what is the separate mention of כרת for a sister there to teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that every extra word in the תורה must teach something. Since the רבנן do not learn 'כרת and not מלקות' from it, they need another use for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? What does it teach?
The Sages, here the side that holds חייבי כריתות get מלקות

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, why do I need karet for his sister?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the רבנן explain the פסוק that רבי יצחק used in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra mention of כרת for a sister teaches according to the רבנן.

steps.title: To count each forbidden relationship separately
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from it that each forbidden relationship counts separately, as רבי יוחנן says: if a person did them all in one העלם, he is חייב for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: To divide them, as רבי יוחנן says: if a person did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is חייב for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the רבנן, the sister verse teaches לחלק, that each forbidden relationship is its own separate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, someone who did many of these sins while unaware might bring only one קרבן. Because the sister is taken out of the group, each forbidden relationship stands alone. So he brings a separate חטאת for each one, as רבי יוחנן rules.

keyTerms.meaning: To divide, meaning each sin counts separately
One lapse of awareness; he did them all without realizing it was forbidden
For each and every one

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same extra mention in the פסוק can be used in different ways: here the רבנן use it for counting sins, while רבי יצחק uses it for the punishment. Steps 9 to 13 refine what exactly the רבנן learn from it.

phrases.english: To divide, in line with Rabbi Yochanan,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the forbidden relationships listed in the תורה.

phrases.english: he is liable for each and every one.
phrases.notes: Liable here means he must bring a separate חטאת for each sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sister verse teaches לחלק: each forbidden relationship needs its own קרבן, as רבי יוחנן says.

steps.title: Where does רבי יצחק learn לחלק?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יצחק used the sister verse for 'כרת and not מלקות,' the גמרא asks where he learns לחלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק, where does he learn לחלק from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the opposite question. רבי יצחק already used the sister verse, so where does he get the rule that each forbidden relationship counts separately?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees with the rule of לחלק. Since one פסוק can usually teach only one thing, רבי יצחק needs a different source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak, from where does he learn dividing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 5, now asking about רבי יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יצחק's source for the rule of לחלק.

steps.title: From the verse about a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns לחלק from 'ואל אשה בנדת טמאתה': a person is חייב for each woman separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'ואל אשה בנדת טמאתה,' to make him חייב for each and every woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק gets לחלק from a different פסוק, the one about a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ואל אשה' (and to a woman) are read as extra. רבי יצחק uses them to teach that each forbidden woman is a separate sin. That leaves the sister verse free to teach 'כרת and not מלקות.'

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
The separation of her impurity, meaning a woman who is a נדה
Each and every woman

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that each forbidden relationship counts separately (לחלק). רבי יצחק learns it from 'ואל אשה,' because he uses the sister verse to teach 'כרת and not מלקות.' Step 10 shows that the רבנן also learn לחלק from 'ואל אשה,' so for them the sister verse teaches something else.

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִוְּאֶל אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טֻמְאָתָהּ,
phrases.english: He derives it from 'And to a woman in the separation of her impurity,'
to make him liable for each and every woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִוְּאֶל אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טֻמְאָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק learns לחלק from the extra words 'ואל אשה' in the פסוק about a נדה.

steps.title: Why not let the רבנן learn separation from the נדה verse too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: they could learn לחלק from the verse 'ואל אשה בנדת טמאתה', just like רבי יצחק does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן too, let them learn it from this verse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the רבנן don't need the extra sister verse to learn that each woman counts separately. The נדה verse that רבי יצחק used already teaches that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the רבנן used the extra כרת by a sister to teach לחלק. But Step 8 showed that the נדה verse already teaches לחלק. So the sister verse seems wasted according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him learn it from this source instead

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too,
let them derive it from this!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the נדה verse from Step 8, 'ואל אשה בנדת טמאתה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יצחק's source from Step 8 to challenge the רבנן's source from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of the sister verse for לחלק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the נדה verse already teaches לחלק, the sister verse is not needed for that.

steps.title: The רבנן agree, so the sister verse needs a new purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the רבנן do learn לחלק from the נדה verse, and then asks again what the extra כרת by a sister is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But then, why do I need the כרת written by a sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the challenge: the רבנן also learn לחלק from the נדה verse. This reopens the question of what the sister verse teaches, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the רבנן take the נדה verse for לחלק, the extra כרת by a sister has no job. So the גמרא has to find a new lesson for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees)
Why do I need it? (what does it teach?)

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
But then, why do I need the כרת of his sister?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי. וְאֶלָּא, כָּרֵת דַּאֲחוֹתוֹ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 9 and brings back the question of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession followed by reopening the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן needed the sister verse to teach לחלק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן learn לחלק from the נדה verse, so the sister verse must teach something else.

steps.title: First suggestion: three different sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the sister verse teaches that he is חייב separately for his sister, his father's sister, and his mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: To make him חייב for his sister, and for his father's sister, and for his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer: the verse teaches that sleeping with three different relatives (in one העלם) makes him bring three קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the three women are three different people. This answer will be challenged in the next step as too obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: To make him liable (here, for a separate קרבן חטאת)

phrases.english: To make him liable for his sister,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: and for his father's sister and for his mother's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְחַיְּיבוֹ עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra כרת by a sister teaches for the רבנן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Separate liability for three different sister-type relatives.

steps.title: That is obvious: different women, different prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion: of course he is חייב three times, since they are three different women and three different איסורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! These are separate bodies and separate names!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the first answer teaches nothing new. Three different women, each with her own איסור, obviously give three separate חיובים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse is not needed to teach something we would know anyway. Since both the women and the names of the איסורים are different, separate liability is automatic.

keyTerms.meaning: That is obvious (so why would a verse be needed?)
Separate bodies: different women
Separate names: different named איסורים

phrases.english: It is obvious!
These are separate bodies,
these are separate names!
phrases.notes: 'Names' means the names of the איסורים: 'sister', 'father's sister', 'mother's sister'.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, הֲרֵי גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין, הֲרֵי שֵׁמוֹת מוּחְלָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the verse teaches liability for three different sisters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separate women and separate איסורים obviously give separate חיובים, so no verse is needed.

steps.title: One woman who is all three relatives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the verse teaches he is חייב three times for one woman who is his sister, his father's sister, and his mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, to make him חייב for his sister who is also his father's sister and also his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the case: it is one woman who fits all three relationships. The verse teaches that even so he is חייב for each relationship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is only one body, so we might think there is only one חיוב. The verse teaches that three different names of איסור still count separately, even with one woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is (also): the same woman fits another relationship

steps.confusionAlert: Step 11 was about three different women. This step is about ONE woman with three relationships to him. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: Rather, to make him liable for his sister
who is his father's sister
who is his mother's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְחַיְּיבוֹ עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 11 after the challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is about three different women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is about one woman who carries three names of איסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that separate names of איסור can create separate חיובים even in one act with one woman.

steps.title: How could such a woman exist?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how one woman could be a man's sister, his father's sister, and his mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real-life case where this could happen. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before accepting that the verse teaches this case, the גמרא makes sure the case is actually possible.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: And how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete case to fit the answer of Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case of one woman who is sister, father's sister and mother's sister

steps.title: A רשע son of a רשע
steps.stepSummary: The case happens in a family of רשעים: a רשע who is the son of a רשע.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a wicked man, son of a wicked man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this happens only through sinful relationships across two generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man has two daughters with his own mother. He then has a son with one of those daughters. That son's other half-sister is his sister (same father), his father's sister (same mother as his father), and his mother's sister.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked man, son of a wicked man

phrases.english: With a wicked man, son of a wicked man.
phrases.notes: The father sinned with his own mother and with his daughter, and the son sins with the other daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case arises from two generations of forbidden relationships.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן: the נדה verse teaches לחלק between women, and the extra כרת by a sister teaches separate חיובים for one woman who is sister, father's sister and mother's sister.

steps.title: Where does רבי יצחק learn the three-names case?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יצחק used the sister verse for 'כרת and not מלקות', the גמרא asks where he learns the one-woman-three-names rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק, from where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי יצחק. His sister verse is already taken, so where does he get the rule from Step 13?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the sister verse teaches the three-names case. רבי יצחק used that verse for a different lesson (Step 4), so he needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak, from where does he derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of Step 13 to רבי יצחק's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יצחק's source for separate חיובים for one woman with three names

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns it from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק learns it through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: a logical קל וחומר, not a verse. It will now bring the ברייתא that shows this קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no verse is free, רבי יצחק uses logic. The details of the קל וחומר come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger case

phrases.english: He derives it from an a fortiori argument,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's question in the meat market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע whether a man with a woman who is his sister, father's sister and mother's sister brings one קרבן or three.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא said, I asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע in the meat market of עימאום, where they went to buy an animal for the feast of רבן גמליאל's son: one who is with his sister who is his father's sister who is his mother's sister, what is the law? Is he חייב only once for all of them, or for each one separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show where the קל וחומר comes from. Here רבי עקיבא asks the exact question of the one-woman case, setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's question has two sides: one act with one woman might mean one קרבן, or the three names might mean three קרבנות. The answer in the next step will use a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A meat market
A feast (here, a wedding feast)
Each and every one separately

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: I asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua
in the meat market of Emmaus,
where they went to buy an animal
for the feast of Rabban Gamliel's son:
One who has relations with his sister

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אָבִיו שֶׁהִיא אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: who is his father's sister who is his mother's sister, what is the law?
Is he liable for all of them only once,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת?
phrases.english: or is he liable for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that contains the קל וחומר mentioned in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That the one-woman-three-names rule comes from a קל וחומר
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי עקיבא's question to רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע

steps.title: The קל וחומר from five נדות
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע answer: we heard that one who is with five נדות in one העלם is חייב for each one, so all the more so here, where there are three names of איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This we did not hear. But we heard that one who is with five נדות in one העלם is חייב for each one. And it seems logical by a קל וחומר: if by נדה, which is one name, he is חייב for each one, here, where there are three names, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages say they have no tradition on this exact case, but they build a קל וחומר from the case of five נדות. This is the source the גמרא first suggests for רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נדה there is only one name of איסור, yet he is חייב for each woman. Here there are three different names, which is an even stronger reason to split the חיוב. So he brings a separate קרבן for each name.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness (he forgot the whole time)
One name of איסור
Is it not all the more so?

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע build a קל וחומר: if one name (נדה) gives a חיוב for each woman, three names surely give three חיובים. This is only the first suggested source for רבי יצחק. Steps 20 to 22 reject it and give him the second 'אחותו' in the פסוק instead.

phrases.english: They said to him: This we did not hear,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ: הַבָּא עַל חָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים נִדּוֹת
phrases.english: but we heard: one who has relations with five menstruating women
in one lapse of awareness
is liable for each and every one,
and the matter appears so by an a fortiori argument:
If a menstruating woman, which is one name,
he is liable for each and every one,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן שֶׁשְּׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת – לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: here, where there are three names, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question from Step 18 and spells out the קל וחומר of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Separate חיוב for each name, learned by קל וחומר from five נדות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's first try at a source for רבי יצחק that keeps the sister verse free for 'כרת and not מלקות'. Steps 21 and 22 show that the קל וחומר fails, and the גמרא gives him a verse instead.

steps.title: The other side rejects the קל וחומר from five נדות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not use the קל וחומר because it can be broken. The five נדות are five separate women, but here there is only one woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side holds that it is a breakable קל וחומר: what is special about נדה? There, the bodies are separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other opinion, the רבנן, does not accept the קל וחומר that רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע used. They say it has a weak spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With five נדות there are five different women, so it makes sense to bring five קרבנות. Here there is only one woman with three names. That difference means the קל וחומר does not hold, so the רבנן need a פסוק instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A קל וחומר that can be broken down by pointing to a difference
Separate bodies, meaning different people
And the other one, meaning the other opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'ואידך' means the רבנן, who learn the rule from a פסוק. It does not mean רבי יצחק, who was just said to use the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means the other opinion, the רבנן. They learn the three-names rule from the word 'his sister' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: It is a breakable קל וחומר:
what is special about נדה?
That there, the bodies are separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the other opinion does not accept the קל וחומר quoted in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from five נדות in one העלם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Five נדות are separate bodies, but the sister case is one woman

steps.title: The same weakness applies to רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the קל וחומר can be broken, then רבי יצחק cannot rely on it either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other side too, this is surely a breakable קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the weakness against רבי יצחק. If the קל וחומר is broken, it should not work for him either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said רבי יצחק learns the three-names rule from the קל וחומר. But the difference just pointed out, separate bodies, is a real flaw. So רבי יצחק needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly, surely
Also, too

phrases.english: And for the other one too,
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' means רבי יצחק.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי וַדַּאי קַל וָחוֹמֶר פְּרִיכָא הוּא!
phrases.english: this is surely a breakable קל וחומר!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הַאי וַדַּאי קַל וָחוֹמֶר פְּרִיכָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the flaw from step 20 to attack step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 17, which says רבי יצחק learns the rule through a קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר with a known flaw cannot be a source for anyone, including רבי יצחק

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns it from the second 'אחותו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its answer. רבי יצחק learns the three-names rule from the word 'his sister' at the end of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learns it from 'his sister' in the end part of the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the קל וחומר and gives רבי יצחק a source in the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 20:17 says 'his sister' twice. רבי יצחק already used the separate mention of כרת in this פסוק to teach כרת and not מלקות. So he learns the one-woman-three-names rule from the second one, at the end of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier answer is being dropped
The end part of a פסוק or a text
He learns it from

phrases.english: Rather, he learns it
from 'his sister' in the end part.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17. The end of that פסוק says 'he uncovered the nakedness of his sister.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by replacing the קל וחומר with a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק relies on the קל וחומר from five נדות
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יצחק learns the three-names rule from the second 'אחותו' in the פסוק

steps.title: What do the רבנן use the second 'אחותו' for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן need the word 'his sister' at the end of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side: why do I need 'his sister' at the end?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the רבנן. They already learn the three-names rule from the first 'his sister', so what is the second one for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word in the תורה should teach something. Since the רבנן have a source already, the second 'אחותו' looks extra for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question asking what an extra word teaches

phrases.english: And the other one,
why do I need 'his sister' in the end part?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question from step 22 onto the other opinion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the second 'אחותו'

steps.title: The second 'אחותו' covers a full sister
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use it to make a man liable for a sister from both his father and his mother. This teaches that we do not punish based on a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: To make him liable for his sister who is the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother, to teach that we do not punish based on logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second 'his sister' adds the case of a full sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names a sister from the father or from the mother. You might think a full sister is obviously included by a קל וחומר. But the תורה writes it anyway, which teaches that a punishment cannot come from a קל וחומר alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of his father and of his mother; a full sister
We do not give a punishment based on a logical derivation like a קל וחומר
To make him liable

steps.whyThisMatters: אין עונשין מן הדין is a basic rule across ש״ס. A punishment needs a written source, not just a logical argument.

phrases.english: To make him liable for his sister
who is the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother,
to teach that we do not punish based on logic.
phrases.notes: 'Logic' here means a קל וחומר. Without this word, you might learn a full sister from a half sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְחַיְּיבוֹ עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ בַּת אָבִיו וּבַת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן, the second 'אחותו' covers a full sister and teaches אין עונשין מן הדין

steps.title: Where does רבי יצחק learn the full sister?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבי יצחק used the second 'אחותו' for something else, so where does he learn liability for a full sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רבי יצחק. Since he used the second 'his sister' for the three-names rule, it asks how he covers the full-sister case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides need a source for the full sister, because a קל וחומר cannot create a punishment. For רבי יצחק the second 'אחותו' is already taken, so he needs another source.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now this means רבי יצחק. The full question is: where does he learn liability for a full sister?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the mirror question of step 23 for רבי יצחק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יצחק's source for liability for a full sister

steps.title: First answer: he learns the punishment from the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: One answer: רבי יצחק learns the punishment from the prohibition. Since the prohibition includes a full sister, so does the punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say he learns the punishment from the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first possible answer for רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a separate verse that forbids a sister, called the אזהרה, and it covers a full sister. רבי יצחק takes that and applies it to the punishment. This counts as learning from a source, not from a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; introduces one possible answer
The punishment
The warning; the verse that forbids the act
He learns, he derives

phrases.english: If you want, say
he learns the punishment from the warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק learns the punishment for a full sister from the אזהרה

steps.title: Second answer begins: he learns it from another source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a second possible answer: רבי יצחק learns the full-sister case from somewhere else. The source comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say he learns it from...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second answer for רבי יצחק. The actual source is given in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא offers another way to find a written source for the full sister. These words only set up the answer; the source itself comes right after.

phrases.english: And if you want, say
he learns it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second, alternative answer to step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Introduces a second source for רבי יצחק (completed in the following text)
